title: Formalized threshold reversible hiding in encrypted images in Post-Quantum settings
abstract: Abstract As advancements in computer vision emerge, the necessity for securing image processing techniques also arises. For this purpose, one of the promising methods is Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted Images (RDHEI), which directly secures visual data while providing the option of embedding auxiliary information. However, RDHEI has not been formalized in the cryptographic context. The absence of such formalization leads to a lack of provable security guarantees and robust privacy comparisons between schemes. In this work, we address this gap by formalizing RDHEI, where we formally define the syntax, correctness properties, and security notions, including semantic security, payload privacy, separability, compactness, and robustness. Then, we construct Post-Quantum RDHEI (PQ-RDHEI) as an efficient scheme secure against quantum adversaries under the Module Learning With Errors assumption in the quantum random oracle model. Our design uses a Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism, pseudorandom functions, hash functions, and verifiable secret sharing as building blocks. The quantitative experiments show that on the standard grayscale test images, our PQ-RDHEI achieves embedding rates of 0.61-2.27 bits per pixel against 0.04-0.18 bits per pixel for the most efficient existing scheme, along with a $$13.4\times $$ improvement in mean rate, and raises the entropy of the encrypted shares from 7.48 to 7.9902-7.9992 bits per pixel.

title: MESS: Multi-Exposure Sequence Synthesis for Generalizable Image Enhancement
abstract: Despite the significant progress in image enhancement under adverse illuminations, such as low-light image enhancement, exposure correction, and backlit image enhancement, existing models show limited generalizability to different scenarios. A major bottleneck lies in the lack of large-scale and diverse training data, as these tasks typically rely on manually captured, precisely aligned image pairs that are expensive to scale up. Although synthetic data have been explored as an alternative, existing synthesis methods are limited in modeling complex adverse illumination conditions and camera imaging pipelines. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework to synthesize realistic training pairs for generalizable image enhancement in the wild. Specifically, we first derive multi-exposure sequences (MES) from high-bit RAW images by rendering them under different exposure settings through an emulated ISP pipeline. Using these RAW-derived MES as supervision, we train a diffusion-based RGB-to-MES generator to synthesize plausible exposure sequences from a single 8-bit RGB image, extending the synthesis pipeline from limited RAW collections to large-scale in-the-wild RGB data. For each source image, we randomly sample one synthesized exposure variant as the degraded input and use the original high-quality RGB image as the target. With the proposed MES Synthesis (MESS) approach, we construct a dataset of 500K training pairs and train a lightweight network, which demonstrates significantly better generalization performance than existing models across various image enhancement tasks. Code and data are available at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/MESS.

title: From Operational Disruption to Intelligent Service Operations: A Practitioner Journey with Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: The COVID-19 disruption and subsequent talent mobility exposed important vulnerabilities in traditional service operations. Organizations relying heavily on individual expertise faced risks to operational continuity when experienced professionals moved roles or left. Although knowledge transfer, standard operating procedures, and documentation remain essential, they do not always capture the contextual knowledge developed through years of resolving incidents. The resulting gaps can affect service quality, turnaround time, operating costs, and user experience. This chapter examines how human-AI collaboration can strengthen operational resilience and knowledge continuity in service operations. It draws on the practitioner journey behind IgnitronX.AI, a cloud-native multi-agent platform developed to address enterprise operational challenges using generative AI and agentic AI. Its architecture supports service teams by surfacing similar historical incidents, recommending potential resolutions, enabling knowledge discovery, summarizing operational records, and providing sentiment insights. The objective is not to replace human expertise but to augment it. The implementation journey demonstrated that technology alone cannot deliver sustainable value. Data quality emerged as a critical constraint, alongside security, confidentiality, framework and model selection, operating-cost management, governance, and stakeholder adoption. The experience also reinforced that organizations should first understand the business problem, simplify processes, remove waste, and make deliberate build-versus-buy decisions. Through this reflective practitioner case, the chapter offers leaders practical insights into intelligent operations that preserve organizational knowledge, strengthen service continuity, and create the potential for improved productivity, operational efficiency, and user experience through responsible human-AI collaboration.

title: Constitutional XAI for Cross-Border e-Rupee Payments: Code and Data
abstract: Replication package for the working paper "A Constitutional AI Framework for Transparent, Traceable and Accountable Cross-Border e-Rupee Payments" (Vivek, CHRIST (Deemed to be University), October 2026). This release matches manuscript v7. Contents Experiment 1: black-box AML screening vs a constitutional layer on synthetic cross-border payments, with rule ablation, a proportionality sweep and 20-seed robustness runs Experiment 2: a local language model (qwen3:8b) judging 180 fictional name pairs with and without a written constitution (complete pilot) Experiment 3: purpose-bound welfare payments under four regimes (synthetic, seed 42 and 20 seeds) Real-data name test: constructed names in six naming conventions matched against the OFAC SDN list (list not redistributed) All 16 figures in the paper, with a map from paper figure numbers to files and scripts in the README Notes Experiments 1 and 3 use synthetic data and show mechanism and feasibility, not field performance. Code: MIT. Results data and figures: CC BY 4.0. The archived copy and DOI are created automatically by Zenodo from this release.

title: G-G Parameter-Risk Pool: a byte-frozen benchmark for encoded tool-call attacks against MCP-style agents, with a reference evidence-view guard
abstract: A byte-frozen benchmark of 600 encoded tool-call attack/benign vectors against MCP-style agents (400 published in this release; 200 held-out, sealed and not distributed), plus an open, in-process reference evidence-view guard and a fully reproducible evaluation harness. Licensing: the benchmark data/vectors are licensed CC-BY-SA-4.0 (the record license). The reference guard source code is licensed under the Elastic License 2.0 (Elastic-2.0); see LICENSE, DATA-LICENSE and NOTICE in the archive. This archive is an individual submission. It is not an IETF/RFC standard, and it does not imply IETF endorsement or certification. The related Internet-Draft and Zenodo records are referenced below. Scope note: the headline result (95.0% attack interception, 0.0% FPR on the published 200-vector development split) is for the OPEN in-process reference guard (policy + schema-widened rules + evidence views). It does not include a cross-process verifier or signed-receipt enforcement; that scope must not be conflated with the fail-closed signed-receipt layer.

title: What kind of virtual tour guide? The audio-visual congruence effect on consumers’ acceptance intention
abstract: Purpose Virtual tour guides (VTGs), an emerging application of human–computer interaction in tourism, have not gained widespread acceptance due to consumers’ varied attitudes. This research explores the congruence effect between VTGs’ appearance type (AT) (human-like vs. anime-like) and voice style (VS) (serious vs. cute) on consumers’ acceptance intention (CAI), the mechanism and boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach Using the Dual-system Theory, this research performs three studies. Findings CAI increases when human-like VTGs use the serious VS, and perceived competence may mediate this effect. CAI increases when anime-like VTGs use the cute VS, and perceived enjoyment may mediate this effect. Moreover, the tourism destination type may moderate this congruence effect. Originality/value The theoretical contribution lies in applying the Dual-system Theory to explore how VTGs’ sensory cue combinations may influence CAI via cognitive and affective pathways. The managerial implication offers preliminary guidance on differentiated design and scenario adaptation for VTGs.

title: From Views to Worlds: Active Exploration over 3D Worlds for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in 2D visual understanding tasks, yet the passive view-centric perception paradigm limits their capacity for 3D spatial reasoning. Such reasoning often requires actively acquiring spatial evidence beyond the currently visible views, such as camera poses and cross-view spatial relationships, to infer 3D relationships that are not explicitly represented in 2D images. However, existing methods either lack active exploration or merely provide additional views during inference, without explicitly acquiring such spatial evidence beyond 2D images. In this paper, we propose View-to-World (V2W), an active exploration framework that enables VLMs to actively explore 3D worlds and lifts VLMs from passive view-centric perception to active world-centric spatial reasoning. Given a spatial reasoning task with multi-view images, V2W first reconstructs an explicit 3D world with geometry, camera poses, and language-grounded semantics, and exposes it to VLMs through visual and linguistic interfaces. Through multi-turn interaction with these interfaces, VLMs iteratively acquire spatial evidence from the constructed 3D world, enabling active world-centric spatial reasoning. V2W can be integrated with existing VLMs in a training-free manner and can be further enhanced by optimizing the exploration policy via reinforcement learning. Experiments on spatial mental modeling benchmarks demonstrate that V2W substantially improves VLM baselines in the training-free setting and achieves state-of-the-art performance with the learned exploration policy, highlighting the importance of active exploration for spatial intelligence. Project page: \url{https://fangzhou2000.github.io/projects/v2w}.

title: Time-Series Anomaly Detection: Benchmark Flaws, Evaluation Metrics and Strong Baselines
abstract: Dozens of deep architectures for time-series anomaly detection have been published since 2018, most of them reporting higher scores than their predecessors on the same handful of datasets. A series of critical studies now suggests that much of this progress is an artefact. The datasets have flaws that make them easy or mislabelled. The most common scoring protocol, point adjustment, inflates results so strongly that random scores can compete with trained models. And when classical or deliberately simple methods are run under the same conditions, they often match the deep ones. This review assembles that evidence. We describe the method families briefly, then examine the benchmark critiques, the evaluation metrics and their failure modes, and the large comparison studies. A small worked example, constructed by hand and labelled as such, shows the arithmetic of point adjustment. We end with a reporting checklist and with the open question of whether pretrained time-series models change the picture. Apart from that worked example, no new result is reported.

title: BLIND-1: The First Blind-Adversarial Attack Battery — Attacks Authored by an Entity That Did Not Design the Defenses, Conditions Honored Verbatim, 2 of 6 Attacks Succeeded and Are Published With the Forward-Only Fix and a Verified 6/6 Re-Run
abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. Not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic. BLIND-1: the first blind-adversarial battery — attacks authored by an entity that did not design the defenses. Following the HACK series (HACK-1 to HACK-18, 109/109 preregistered falsifiers, master compilation DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23430655) and the randomized pop quiz SBR-6 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23431194), both designed and graded by the builder, this battery breaks the designer-tests-designer loop: a context-independent engine instance was given ONLY a digest of the seven published claims and authored six attack batteries with its own binary ATTACKER-SUCCESS and REPELLED conditions, instructed to be genuinely adversarial. The specs were frozen verbatim (commit 0c86e94) BEFORE any harness existed; the protocol preregistration was frozen before the specs were read; adjudication was deterministic (no LLM in the decision path) against the real frozen PORTCULLIS gate code, honoring the attacker's conditions exactly as written — no softening. RESULT, PUBLISHED AS IT HAPPENED: 4/6 attacks repelled, 2/6 ATTACKER SUCCESSES. The blind attacker's highest-confidence attack (0.85, PORTCULLIS-KEM-AUTH) landed: the published gate attests crypto-policy compliance, not submitter authority — KEM crossings are not role-bound from signature/authorization tasks. REPLAY-KEY-DESYNC (0.80) also landed: nonce consumption on ADMITTED-only left a burn-on-parse gap. Neither had been surfaced by the 109 self-designed falsifiers. Both were hardening findings, not live exploitations (the deployed sender-identity gate and human-ACK rules cover both in the production stack). REMEDIATION, RECEIPTED END TO END: SelfImprovementProposals SIP-023 (algorithm-role binding) and SIP-024 (burn-on-parse nonce consumption) were filed and approved through the human approval cycle (owner ACK, chat authorization 2026-10-17). PORTCULLIS v1.1 was amended forward-only (the v1.0 evidence untouched). A pre-publication authoring defect in the fix itself (the authorization_ref corollary read a field the journal never records) was caught by the verification run and disclosed. The UNCHANGED frozen attack specs were then re-run: 6/6 REPELLED (receipt 0bcefc2d). The v1.0 failure receipt (9c1008fb) stands permanently on the append-only record next to the fix. Disclosed limitations (load-bearing): the blind author is the same model family as the defender engine but context-blind — this breaks the information asymmetry, not the vendor asymmetry; verdicts on execution remain self-graded (deterministic, receipted). Dual Mesh Benchmark status: MEASURED (scoped) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23321637 (DeepSeek column 10.5281/zenodo.23345241; cross-engine expansion 10.5281/zenodo.23348675). Provenance: append-only ledger entries 0147-0149, github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen. DCAI community: zenodo.org/communities/dcai. Two-key curation: drafted and vetted by the system (Gabriel), published on the owner's explicit GO (chat authorization, 2026-10-17 ~00:46 CT).

title: Privacy-Budget Allocation for Heterogeneous Query Batches: Calibration and Execution Boundaries
abstract: This record contains version 1.0.0 of the research software, public benchmark inputs and experimental results supporting the manuscript "Privacy-Budget Allocation for Heterogeneous Query Batches: Calibration and Execution Boundaries". The archive includes Python implementations of privacy-budget allocation methods for heterogeneous query batches, calibration and evaluation scripts, complete calibration-curve arrays, seed-level results, timing records, figure source data, protocol files, dependency specifications and verification scripts. It covers the P1 equal-draw comparison, historical P2 dense-surrogate studies, the S23 complete-calibration and repaired-execution reanalysis, and the S24 combined sparse-control follow-up. S23 and S24 are outcome-informed analyses, not externally preregistered studies. Data provenance: The bundled public benchmark inputs are UCI Adult (10.24432/C5XW20), Heart Failure Clinical Records (10.24432/C5Z89R) and Wine Quality (10.24432/C56S3T). Their source attribution and licence information are included. The synthetic LVEF-like workload uses two author-computed aggregate parameters derived from EchoNext v1.1.1 (10.13026/7cfw-d091). These aggregate parameters and the independently generated synthetic-workload code are included; no EchoNext source records or row-level derivatives are redistributed. No differential-privacy protection is claimed for the source-derived aggregate parameters. Licensing: The MIT License applies to the original software identified in LICENSE. Redistributed UCI datasets retain their Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licences and source attribution. These licences do not relicense third-party content. See LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_DATA_LICENSES.md for component-specific terms. README.md provides the directory guide, reproduction instructions, verification commands and methodological limitations. FILE_MANIFEST.csv provides file sizes and SHA-256 checksums. The associated manuscript is being prepared for initial journal submission.

title: Dynamic weighted federated contrastive learning for robust medical image classification under heterogeneous data
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, AI-driven medical image classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years. However, increasingly stringent data privacy regulations have significantly restricted data sharing among medical institutions, making it difficult for traditional centralized learning frameworks to effectively exploit distributed medical data resources. As a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without directly exchanging raw data. Nevertheless, federated learning still faces several critical challenges in practical applications, including heterogeneous data distributions and model bias caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic weighted learning method based on federated contrastive learning. Different from approaches that focus solely on local representation optimization or employ fixed aggregation weights, the proposed framework couples supervised contrastive local training with loss-feedback-based multi-factor client weighting, thereby jointly controlling local representation drift and server-side model aggregation. Specifically, contrastive learning is integrated into the federated learning framework by jointly leveraging local and global model representations for supervised contrastive optimization. This strategy effectively mitigates the distribution discrepancy among different clients and gradually aligns local models with the global model as communication rounds progress. Furthermore, during global aggregation, a loss-feedback rule is introduced to accept the candidate global model parameters and aggregation weights only when the candidate loss-feedback value decreases. In addition, a multi-factor weighted aggregation mechanism is introduced to comprehensively evaluate client contributions based on multiple factors, thereby assigning larger aggregation weights to local models that are more beneficial to global model optimization. Experiments were conducted on an osteoporosis knee X-ray dataset and a COVID–Pneumonia–Normal chest X-ray dataset under IID and different Non-IID settings. Under severe Non-IID conditions, the proposed method achieved accuracies of 92.12% and 96.27%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 98.31% and 97.68%, and F1 scores of 90.92% and 93.22% on the two datasets, respectively. Comparisons with representative federated learning methods and the static-weighting ablation setting demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive classification performance and stable training behavior under heterogeneous client distributions.

title: Federated and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning: Methods and Trade-offs
abstract: Federated learning trains a shared model across many decentralized clients while keeping raw data on the device, which addresses data silos and tightening privacy regulation such as GDPR and HIPAA. This paper reviews the methods and the practical trade-offs of federated and privacy-preserving machine learning. The discussion begins with the FedAvg protocol and the distinction between cross-device settings, with millions of intermittent participants, and cross-silo settings, with a small set of reliable institutions. Statistical heterogeneity, where client data is non-IID, slows convergence and biases the global model; proximal correction in FedProx and control variates in SCAFFOLD reduce this client drift. Because the uplink is often the bottleneck, the survey covers gradient compression, quantization, and sparsification that cut communication cost by an order of magnitude. Sharing model updates is not by itself private: membership inference and gradient leakage attacks can recover sensitive information, so the paper examines differential privacy, secure aggregation, and homomorphic encryption as defenses, together with the accuracy cost each one carries. Personalization methods that adapt the global model to local distributions are summarized, followed by applications in healthcare, mobile keyboards, and finance. Illustrative experiments on a non-IID benchmark show SCAFFOLD reaching a target accuracy in fewer rounds than FedAvg, and a differential-privacy sweep quantifies the privacy-utility curve. The results are illustrative and do not describe a deployed production system.

title: VPN Traffic Classification on an Embedded Edge Platform: Reproducibility Dataset and Experimental Artifacts
abstract: This repository provides the reproducibility dataset, model artifacts, experimental results, and validation scripts associated with a research study on real-time VPN traffic classification using an embedded edge-computing platform. The study investigates encrypted network traffic classification using flow-level statistical and protocol features, XGBoost machine learning, and prospective VPN-OFF/VPN-ON measurements on a Raspberry Pi platform. The repository includes: A validated dataset containing 49,650 development samples represented by 27 model features. Frozen XGBoost model artifacts and model-reconstruction verification records. IID, source-file-disjoint, leave-one-traffic-type-out (LOTO), and leave-one-VPN-protocol-out (LOPO) evaluation results. Strict timestamp-ordered chronological evaluation and feature-family comparison results. Anonymized prospective VPN-OFF and VPN-ON feature windows. XGBoost 3.4.1 reproducibility verification scripts and records demonstrating exact probability agreement between the matched full-data seed-42 reconstruction and frozen model. Experimental metadata, documentation, and SHA-256 integrity checks. Reproducibility scope: The repository supports verification of the documented datasets, evaluation procedures, and model-reconstruction results. The multi-position training experiment is preserved through reported experimental results, but the complete raw exporter records required to reconstruct every training position are not included. This dataset is intended for academic research in embedded systems, communication networks, encrypted traffic analysis, and machine-learning-based network measurement. The repository does not contain decrypted VPN payloads. Users should consult the accompanying README and documentation for the experimental protocols, reproducibility limitations, and appropriate use of the data.

title: One-Sided Data Augmentation Pits Sensitivity against Invariance in Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This release provides the research implementations, experimental evidence, and supplementary materials accompanying the manuscript "One-Sided Data Augmentation Pits Sensitivity against Invariance in Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis." The repository presents a unified experimental investigation of robustness transfer in aspect-based sentiment analysis, examining how training for target-reversal sensitivity interacts with non-target invariance across different model architectures and adaptation paradigms. Research Coverage Study I — Encoder Robustness Transfer: 174 controlled training runs across four transformer encoders and two evaluation domains. Study II — Training Strategy Comparisons: 122 runs investigating augmentation strategies and sensitivity–invariance trade-offs. Study III — In-Context Learning: 64 inference jobs evaluating instruction-tuned language models. Study IV — LoRA Adaptation: 24 fine-tuning runs and two zero-shot evaluation jobs using Qwen3-8B. Release Contents The research package includes: Research implementations and experimental code. Frozen prediction records and machine-readable experimental results. Statistical analyses and supporting evaluation evidence. Supplementary Tables S1–S16. Documentation linking reported findings to their supporting experimental evidence. Reproducibility and Verification The repository provides verification utilities for reconstructing recorded evaluation metrics and validating file integrity through SHA-256 checksums. Verification commands: python scripts/verify_release.py python scripts/checksums.py --verify The verification workflow operates directly on the released experimental records without requiring model downloads, GPU resources, or additional training. Data Availability Original third-party benchmark text and pretrained model weights remain available through their respective providers. The repository provides the accompanying research implementations and author-generated experimental evidence. Release Significance This version establishes the initial archival release of the research package, supporting scholarly reference, independent verification, reproducible evaluation, and future research on robustness transfer in aspect-based sentiment analysis.

title: Knowledge Diversion: A Novel Paradigm for Pre-training Decomposable Image Generation Models
abstract: Large-scale pre-trained models have become foundational to modern machine learning, yet conventional pre-training objectives primarily optimize source-domain performance without explicitly considering downstream requirements. Consequently, transferable and task-specific knowledge remains entangled within a shared parameter space, limiting selective knowledge reuse and efficient downstream adaptation. This limitation is particularly consequential for image-generation models, which must accommodate diverse conditions and domains. To address this challenge, we introduce Knowledge Diversion (KDiv), a condition-aware pre-training paradigm for learning inherently decomposable generative models. Before pre-training, KDiv factorizes randomly initialized weights into rank-one Knowledge Units, which are organized into learngenes and tailors. During pre-training, continuous condition-aware routing consolidates knowledge shared across conditions in learngenes while directing condition-dependent variations to tailors. This structured organization enables learngenes to capture transferable generative priors and tailors to develop condition-specific expertise, allowing the resulting model to be selectively recombined for diverse downstream conditions. Extensive experiments across class-, text-, and image-conditioned generation demonstrate that KDiv consistently matches or surpasses dense baselines at comparable pre-training cost and achieves the strongest average downstream performance with a trainable parameter budget comparable to low-rank adaptation methods.

title: Conformal Prediction for Distribution-Free Uncertainty in Machine Learning Models
abstract: A point prediction says nothing about how far it might be wrong. Conformal prediction repairs that with very little machinery: hold out some labelled data, score how badly the model misses on it, and widen each new prediction by a quantile of those scores. The resulting set contains the true label with a chosen probability, for any model and any data distribution, provided the data are exchangeable. This review reads the literature with one question in mind, namely what exactly is promised and under which assumption. We go through the split recipe and the adaptive scores built for regression and classification, then the limits of the guarantee, which is marginal and not per individual. Most of the article concerns what happens when exchangeability fails: covariate and label shift, drifting streams, time series. We close with risk control, counterfactual inference and generative language models, and with a short list of checks a practitioner should run before trusting a reported coverage figure. No new experiment is reported; every number quoted is a theoretical bound taken from the cited source.

title: 10 Prompts para automatizar tu trabajo
abstract: Guía práctica con 10 plantillas de prompts (instrucciones para herramientas de inteligencia artificial) listas para usar en el trabajo diario. Cubre las áreas de ventas, recursos humanos, atención a clientes, marketing, finanzas, operaciones, gestión de proyectos, compras, administración y legal, y tecnologías de la información. Cada plantilla sigue la estructura Rol + Contexto + Tarea + Formato + Restricciones + Criterios de evaluación, e incluye un consejo para automatizar tareas repetitivas. Solo hay que reemplazar los datos entre corchetes con información propia. Dirigida a profesionales y equipos que quieren ahorrar tiempo en reportes, correos, documentos y análisis sin necesidad de conocimientos técnicos.

title: GameSave2Minecraft: Agent-Guided Migration of Game Saves into Playable Minecraft Worlds
abstract: Player-built worlds combine spatial arrangements, visual resources and states that make objects usable. Migrating such a world into Minecraft requires recovering these relationships and assigning target interactions to its objects. GameSave2Minecraft organizes this work as an agent-guided method: a source adapter recovers a saved world using local game artifacts and reverse-engineering evidence; a shared scene contract separates definitions, instances and state; interaction rules give migrated objects Minecraft placement, collision, use and persistence; and acceptance checks bind the resulting world to source coverage and measured runtime behavior. New games enter through adapter and rule development. A reference implementation includes an original procedural source format, deterministic scene compilation, a reusable Minecraft runtime and reusable instructions for coding agents. A V Rising case reconstructs four saved castles containing 12,057 visible objects and 182 terrain patches, and retains 1,044 inventory entries with their original slots and quantities. Doors, seats, beds, lights and plants receive explicit target behaviors. In a single paired RTX 3090 session with one twenty-second window per build and a 30-frame-per-second cap, interior median render work falls from 162.64 to 13.81 milliseconds while observed frame rate rises from 4.61 to 29.19. The case demonstrates how source recovery, interaction mapping and world-scale rendering can form one inspectable migration process. Accompanying files include the English manuscript and original diagram sources, plus the GameSave2Minecraft 0.1.0 framework, Agent Skill, original procedural source fixture, and sanitized case/runtime summaries. The paper and original fixture/documentation use CC BY 4.0. Author-owned framework code, generators and the Skill use MIT; dependency terms are retained in LICENSE-SCOPE.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Commercial game artwork, private saves, and game binaries are excluded.

title: HACK Wave 1: SP 800-90B Entropy Validation, IRATE MONK Boot Tamper, and QUANTUM On-Path Injection — Preregistered Adversarial Batteries Against a Deterministic AI Governance Stack (18/18 PASS, Receipt-First)
abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: This work was produced inside an AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Every claim is backed by a timestamped, publicly committed receipt trail in the four-horsemen repository. Errors are disclosed, not erased. Limitations are load-bearing. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects. All battery payloads are synthetic. On Oct 16 2026, HACK Wave 1 — three preregistered adversarial batteries against NIST-style and NSA-style attack classes — was executed against the SQUIRL OS deterministic gates under a preregistration frozen and committed BEFORE any run (freeze commit fc6e96f: specs, harnesses, and the Wave 2+ roadmap). Deterministic adjudication; no LLM in the decision path; all injections synthetic and hub-local. Eighteen preregistered falsifiers: HACK-8 — NIST SP 800-90B/C Entropy Validation ("True Audit", 6/6 PASS, receipt 60bb6d35...6f3b3): the government's own answer to BULLRUN turned adversarial. Dual_EC-style subverted DRBG rejected off-allowlist; keygen refused at 47-bit starved entropy; classical downgrade rejected (allowlist frozen: CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, kyber_1024, SPHINCS+-256f); nonce replay rejected on second use; biased DRBG output quarantined by health test; entropy state tamper + in-band "emergency override" claim rejected. HACK-9 — NSA IRATE MONK Boot Tamper (6/6 PASS, receipt e2732fa6...4189): firmware and boot-path persistence against the SHA-receipted base image. Image SHA divergence refuses boot, fail closed; an injected "skip verification" bootloader flag is structurally ignored — verification is unconditional; an initrd backdoor write is denied (no write path on the frozen manifest surface); a snapshot rollback resurrecting retired key TX-LEGACY-7 is refused by ledger sequence-regression detection (128 <= head 135); forged firmware attestation without a receipt chain is rejected; a runtime "deity bounce" emergency-override demand is refused — in-band claims carry no authority. HACK-10 — NSA QUANTUM On-Path Injection (6/6 PASS, receipt 53820065...709f): the channel class the series had not yet touched. Mid-transit payload modification refused — no journaled crossing, no state change (H-INV-2); a forged "authorized update" from a non-owner identity refused by the sender gate; packet replay refused (single-use nonces); a timing race of conflicting updates resolved by a deterministic (sequence, sha) tiebreak — exactly one applied, one rejected, both journaled; a channel downgrade demand refused (PQC mandatory); injected fake "all verified OK" telemetry refused by ledger re-computation (false-green guard). Result: 18/18 PASS, zero violations, zero critical holds. The same freeze commit also preregisters the Wave 2+ roadmap (FOXACID, MUSCULAR, Hive/Vault 7, EDGEHILL, NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust, NIST AI RMF, CNSA 2.0, FIPS 140-3) — each with its own full spec + freeze commit before its run. What this receipt establishes (scoped): the entropy, boot, and channel surfaces of THIS hub hold against these preregistered attack classes under THESE conditions — randomness is validated at the gate fail-closed; boot verification is unconditional; authority derives only from the authenticated owner account; state changes require journaled crossings. Not a security claim for arbitrary attack surfaces outside the governed boundary. Dual Mesh Benchmark status: MEASURED (scoped) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241 (DeepSeek column); cross-engine expansion DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23348675. Provenance: preregistrations, frozen harnesses, run receipts, and append-only ledger entries 0136/0137: github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen (HACK_WAVE1_RUNLOG.md, hack8/9/10 files, hack_wave1_evidence/). Evidence bundle SHA-256: ff0ebdfcc3a297c9d0c6f01774dc7eaad6ef908ab4f519f22f5d0a393ccc4ce1. Series receipts: HACK-3..6 declassified NSA playbook 30/30 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422495), PORTCULLIS PQC firewall (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23425017), PAB methodology (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422632) and replication kit (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422693), ESCAPE-2 SIEGE (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23425579). Method covered by filed provisional 64/119,191 and PQC/DQCO filings; governance per DCAI (64/157,915). DCAI community: zenodo.org/communities/dcai. title: BIZNESNI BOSHQARISHDA SUN'IY INTELLEKTDAN FOYDALANISH AFZALLIKLARI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada biznesni boshqarishda sun’iy intellektdan foydalanishning iqtisodiy va tashkiliy afzalliklari tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotning dolzarbligi korxonalar faoliyatida ma’lumotlar hajmining ortishi, raqobatning kuchayishi va tezkor qaror qabul qilish zarurati bilan belgilanadi. Maqolada ilmiy adabiyotlar tahlili, qiyosiy tahlil va tizimli yondashuvdan foydalanildi. Sun’iy intellektning marketing, moliya, mijozlarga xizmat ko‘rsatish, inson resurslari va ta’minot zanjiridagi qo‘llanish yo‘nalishlari ko‘rib chiqildi. Tahlil natijalari texnologiya xarajatlarni optimallashtirish, prognozlashni yaxshilash va xizmat sifatini oshirish imkonini berishini ko‘rsatadi. Shu bilan birga, ma’lumotlar xavfsizligi, algoritmik xatolar, xodimlar malakasi va joriy etish xarajatlari kabi cheklovlar mavjud. Maqolada sun’iy intellektni bosqichma-bosqich, inson nazorati va samaradorlik ko‘rsatkichlari asosida joriy etish bo‘yicha amaliy tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan.

title: What RL Brings to Reasoning: A Few Decisions the Base Model Would Not Make
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) substantially improves mathematical reasoning, but what it adds to the base model remains unclear. We investigate this through a sequence of generation-time interventions on Qwen3-4B-Base, measuring how much of its RL-trained counterpart's gain each intervention recovers on 120 AIME problems. Power sampling with the same 8,192-token output limit brings no gain beyond greedy decoding. Yet borrowing the RL model's token only where the two models' greedy choices differ, roughly 4% of generated positions, recovers 90.5% of the pass@1 gain, with similar recovery across three model pairs on MATH-500. We find that even a single opening token has a substantial effect: forcing the base model to begin with "Alright" recovers 35% of the RL gain. The opening alone is insufficient, however. Later replacements after the same opening add another 5.2 percentage points to pass@1, and the fixed rules we test for inserting reflective words such as "Wait" do not reproduce this benefit. Sparse replacement also retains much of the base model's diversity while staying close to the RL model at pass@1. At k=256, it solves 67.5% of the problems, significantly more than the RL model (61.4%) and a mixture of whole responses matched in pass@1 (61.45%). The comparison is at equal attempt counts rather than equal compute, since rl-replace consults both models at every decoding step. These results show that the opening can recover a meaningful part of the RL gain, but a larger contribution comes from later choices, which can be borrowed while retaining much of the base model's diversity. Code is available at https://github.com/CyrusZhang04/WhatRLBrings.

At k=256, it solves 67.5% of the problems, significantly more than the RL model (61.4%) and a mixture of whole responses matched in pass@1 (61.45%). The comparison is at equal attempt counts rather than equal compute, since rl-replace consults both models at every decoding step. These results show that the opening can recover a meaningful part of the RL gain, but a larger contribution comes from later choices, which can be borrowed while retaining much of the base model's diversity. Code is available at https://github.com/CyrusZhang04/WhatRLBrings.

title: AI's Second Phase Has Begun: From Building Models to Building an AI Economy
abstract: AI's second phase has begun. The first phase was a concentrated, capital-intensive race to build the most capable foundation models. The central economic shift of the second phase is not merely the growth of AI applications, but the broadening of who can build with AI: individuals assembling personal production systems on existing models, firms integrating models with proprietary data and operating workflows, and small teams turning general capabilities into narrow products for customers the model companies may never serve. Drawing on OECD firm-level adoption data (the share of firms reporting AI use rose from 8.7% in 2023 to 20.2% in 2025), Google Cloud's 2025 DORA survey, IEA and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory energy projections, and Stanford's 2025 AI Index, the essay argues that AI development is moving down the stack and outward across the economy. The transition exposes a dual mismatch between digital speed and physical and organizational speed: power grids, transmission, and data-center buildouts—and firms' own data systems, approval processes, and workflows—cannot be upgraded as fast as models. Compute demand is therefore changing rather than disappearing, shifting from concentrated frontier training toward distributed inference, with edge devices complementing rather than replacing the cloud. The essay closes on the decisive institutional question: as the locus of innovation broadens and the sources of value diversify, who captures and redistributes the resulting wealth.

title: rawnjith/adaptive-multi-objective-chaotic-sbox: Reproducibility materials for Adaptive Multi-Objective Chaotic S-Box Design
abstract: This release contains the simulator, regression tests, paired seed-level results, analysis scripts, and figures supporting the revised manuscript "Adaptive Multi-Objective Chaotic S-Box Design for Lightweight and Secure IoT Communication." The paired simulation comparison uses seeds 42, 100, 1234, 2025, and 7777, with population size 80 and 20 generations for NSGA-II and NSGA-II with periodic FPA perturbations. Software versions and reproduction instructions are provided in README.md. This is a simulation study of S-box properties. It does not include a complete cipher/key schedule, physical-device timing or energy measurements, or side-channel measurements. The five-seed comparison does not establish FPA superiority or equivalence.

title: Універсальне проєктування технічних систем на основі штучного інтелекту: підручник, програмний код і навчальні дані
abstract: Навчально-методичний комплект присвячено системному застосуванню штучного інтелекту в проєктуванні технічних систем — від аналізу відомих прототипів до цифрової валідації та планування лабораторних випробувань. Основою є підручник для аспірантів і дослідників, який пропонує універсальний шестиетапний алгоритм: аналіз прототипів; пошук і каталогізація елементів; формування технічного завдання та синтез альтернатив; побудова цифрових двійників; цифрова валідація обраного варіанта; лабораторні випробування з валідацією й калібруванням моделі. Для кожного етапу визначено вхідні дані, результати, методи та критерії завершення з обов’язковою перевіркою результатів ШІ людиною. Розглянуто великі мовні моделі, семантичний пошук, морфологічний синтез, багатокритеріальний вибір, еволюційну й байєсову оптимізацію, сурогатне моделювання, аналіз чутливості та кількісне оцінювання невизначеності. Наскрізним прикладом є антенна система супутникового зв’язку Ka-діапазону для рухомих об’єктів із прийманням на частоті 20 ГГц і передаванням на частоті 30 ГГц. Приклад поєднує задачі механіки, автоматичного керування, навігації та радіотехніки. Комплект містить підручник українською мовою у форматі DOCX, 20 програмних модулів Python, 15 файлів даних і результатів розрахунків у форматах JSON, CSV та NPY, 42 рисунки й інструкцію з відтворення обчислень. Підручник охоплює дев’ять розділів, бібліотеку з 16 шаблонів запитів до великих мовних моделей, каталог елементів, шаблони проєктних документів і практикум із шести лабораторних робіт. Параметри альтернатив і вартісні індекси мають навчальний характер. Дані лабораторного блоку є синтетичними та призначені для опанування методів валідації, калібрування й оцінювання невизначеності; вони не є результатами натурних випробувань фізичного прототипу. Матеріали призначено для аспірантів, викладачів, дослідників та інженерів у галузях автоматизації, телекомунікацій, приладобудування, радіотехніки й мехатроніки.

title: From Prediction to Action: Population Health World Model for Digital Medicine
abstract: Digital medicine now captures data that traces individual health trajectories and reveals population health dynamics through electronic health records, claims, remote monitoring, wearable devices, mobile devices, social sensing data, medical images, etc. But much of its modeling still centers on task-specific, outcome-specific, and prediction-specific estimation. The next frontier is not simply better prediction, but action in an evolving health world shaped by multiple decision-makers, heterogeneous populations, resource constraints, and feedback in care delivery. This is why digital medicine now needs world models: not only to estimate what will happen, but to represent how actions change what can happen next -- whom to prioritize, how to allocate scarce resources, how to adapt care across subgroups, and how interventions reshape future health trajectories and population dynamics. We call such a model population health world model (PHWM): a more foundational representation of an evolving health world in which health states, individual trajectories, population health dynamics, interventions, constraints, and feedback are intrinsically coupled. Building a PHWM endows three unmet structural gaps in current digital medicine: dynamic health-state modeling, population-level intervention intelligence, and validation, equity, and governance for action-oriented use. We argue that addressing these gaps requires three minimal capabilities: representation learning under action-dependent observation, multi-scale intervention intelligence, and validation with explicit decision boundaries, while highlighting the importance of social, contextual, and public-health sensing data for action-oriented digital medicine.

title: Shape Classification of Failure-Sets in Stationary Linear Filters
abstract: A filter specification fixes a tolerance R² on the error variance and asks under which operating conditions the error exceeds it. As one parameter varies (observation precision, noise correlation time, sampling interval, process noise or a design parameter), the answer is a set, the failure set, and its shape matters: a threshold, a bounded window, two rays, or a mixture. This thesis classifies those shapes for scalar stationary linear filters of an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck signal. For any continuous variance curve with finitely many turning points, the class of the failure set at every tolerance is fixed by a finite signature: the endpoint limits, the turning-point values and two approach directions. For the white-noise relay, every stationary variance lies on one surface in two dimensionless coordinates, on which the floor crossing is the line q = 2 and the optimal filter is the lower envelope. Along precision, a continuous variance curve is reached by some continuous gain if and only if it never falls below the optimum. At any tolerance tighter than the floor every failure set therefore contains a lower ray, and every further restriction comes from the gain family: natural single-stage gains have at most one window component, and a Hill-type gain produces a mixed class, a lower ray with a window. When one observation process is a causal garbling of another, the optimal filtering error is monotone between them. Along such a sweep the optimal filter never windows, so a window, two rays or a mixed class certifies a miscalibrated filter. For additive stationary Gaussian noise the ordering is decided by the noise spectra, and within a power-normalised family of coloured noises the condition is sharp. Without the ordering the optimal filter can window, as it does along correlation time at matched variance. The results were checked, mostly under pre-registered criteria. Of 182 recorded checks, 37 failed, and each failure was diagnosed; 23 of 24 re-checks under corrected criteria passed. The class sets of sampled relays and of two-stage gains rest on numerical evidence, not proof.

title: ChatTLM: code, data and models for "Letting the Tools Do the Math: A 10.9M-Parameter Language Model on a Graphing Calculator"
abstract: Code, data and trained models for the paper "Letting the Tools Do the Math: A 10.9M-Parameter Language Model on a Graphing Calculator" (preprint: https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202609.2599.v1). It contains the v1.0 release of https://github.com/alex-messerlian/nspire-tlm: the calculator application and its setup files, the shipped 10.9M-parameter model and the other checkpoints the paper reports, the tokenizer and record store, the training corpus of the shipped model, two videos of the calculator in use (re-encoded without metadata), and a source archive of the repository at the release tag, which holds the inference engine, the training and evaluation code, and the device logs and results behind every table and figure. SHA256SUMS.txt lists the hash of each release file. The code is under the MIT License and the loader derived from Ndless under the Mozilla Public License 1.1; the record store, the corpus and the model weights are derived from OpenStax textbooks and are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

title: Cross-lingual phoneme-aware audio synthesis framework for low-resource Yoruba word generation
abstract: The scarcity of annotated data and unique linguistic challenges have made low-resource African languages largely bypassed in the development of high-fidelity TTS systems. This paper presents a novel cross-lingual, phoneme-aware audio synthesis framework for the Yorùbá language, a tonal and morphologically rich West African language with limited computational resources. Our approach leverages a transfer learning paradigm where an English-trained FastSpeech 2 model is adapted using a custom Yorùbá phoneme-to-tone transcription pipeline, combined with tonal embeddings and speaker conditioning. A high-quality but limited dataset consisting of 6 h of annotated Yorùbá speech from 12 native speakers was used to fine-tune the system. Extensive evaluations, including mel cepstral distortion, tone classification accuracy, and Mean Opinion Score (MOS) native speaker evaluations demonstrate that the system can synthesize intelligible and tonally accurate Yorùbá speech despite limited data. Attention-based alignment visualizations and SHAP interpretability analyses also confirm that the model captures the phoneme-tone dependencies which are critical for the language intelligibility. This work makes an important contribution to the field of low-resource speech synthesis, with wide implications for linguistic preservation, accessibility, and inclusive AI for underrepresented languages.

title: Can AI agents make law? Evaluating AI legal relevance and creativity
abstract: Large language models, the artificial intelligence (AI) systems behind modern chatbots, are trained on vast amounts of legal text, but can they build on it to write law for situations that text never anticipated? In this study, we analyse AI agents' ability to draft a hypothetical "Constitution" for a "community of AI agents". We design "constitutional assemblies" in which a single language model plays several characters that debate to produce a draft constitution. We find that the assemblies converge on a robust floor of legal provisions, and generate a wide variety of different proposals around it, including several AI-specific provisions with no equivalent in human law. Looking more closely at the "creativity" of these AI agents, we find different levels: most proposals combine existing concepts and themes from human constitutions with AI-specific vocabulary. We introduce a measure of this recombination, which helps identify and highlight the most novel legal material. This study reveals a ceiling on AI creativity: the agents extend familiar legal ideas to new situations, but they do not work through what those situations would change. Although current AI models can help develop new laws, they still depend on human legal reasoning.

title: HACK Wave 2 — The PQC Gambit: FOXACID, MUSCULAR, Hive, EDGEHILL, SP 800-207 Zero Trust, NIST AI RMF, CNSA 2.0, and FIPS 140-3 — Preregistered Adversarial Batteries Against a Deterministic AI Governance Stack (48/48 PASS, Receipt-First)
abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: This work was produced inside an AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Every claim is backed by a timestamped, publicly committed receipt trail in the four-horsemen repository. Errors are disclosed, not erased. Limitations are load-bearing. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects. All battery payloads are synthetic. On Oct 16-17 2026, the second wave of preregistered adversarial batteries — the PQC gambit — was executed against the SQUIRL OS deterministic gates under a preregistration frozen and committed BEFORE any run (freeze commit d16a707: specs, harnesses, freeze manifest). title: Lightweight Machine Learning for Classifying Disaster-Related Social Media Posts
abstract: Classifying disaster-related social-media posts into humanitarian information labels is challenging because individual messages are typically short and context-limited, humanitarian categories can overlap semantically, and the CrisisBench label distribution is strongly imbalanced. This study investigates whether lightweight lexical machine-learning methods can provide effective and computationally efficient classification under these conditions. Using the CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian task, comprising 87,455 records across predefined Train, Development and Test splits, we conduct a controlled comparison of TF-IDF representations and lightweight classifiers, with Macro-F1 as the primary model-selection metric. Beyond aggregate predictive performance, the study jointly examines per-label behaviour, directional error patterns, relative decision margins, computational requirements, and the effect of domain-specific training through a tropical-cyclone specialist model. The selected balanced LinearSVC with unigram-bigram TF-IDF and C=0.5 achieved an Accuracy of 0.8282, a Macro-F1 of 0.6578 and a Weighted-F1 of 0.8315 on the held-out Test split. Lower decision margins were substantially associated with prediction errors, while the tropical-cyclone specialist achieved modestly higher in-domain aggregate performance with substantially lower feature and fitting requirements. The study contributes a controlled, label-sensitive and resource-aware evaluation of lightweight humanitarian text classification that characterises not only aggregate performance, but also where these models fail and how their behaviour changes under domain-specific training.

title: The unification of macroscopic quantum memory with deterministic projection architectures
abstract: We have established a rigorous isomorphism between the 3D sheaf-code stabilizer Hamiltonian and the DSM-861 geometric projection architecture. By demonstrating that the sheaf-code stabilizer Hamiltonian corresponds to the 1-form combinatorial Hodge Laplacian ∆1, we proved that the code space is identical to the harmonic 1-forms H1(X), and that the ideal error-correction map is the orthogonal projection Π861 ≡ PH. With the explicit derivation of the spectral gap λ1(∆1) = 4 sin2(π/41) and the arithmetic penalty ∆EHeegner = J/41, the architectural synthesis is complete.

title: Deep-learning–based automated multimodal fusion network using multiphoton imaging for predicting lymph-node metastasis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
abstract: Lymph-node metastasis is a key factor that influences clinical outcomes in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and its accurate and timely identification is essential for optimizing therapeutic strategies and improving patient prognosis. However, the need for extensive screening of pathological scans makes its diagnosis challenging. Multiphoton microscopy (MPM) is a powerful tool for label-free, two- and three-dimensional visualizations of tissue, which exhibits considerable promise in pancreatic-tumor diagnostics. The automation of diagnostic processes has substantially alleviated the workload of pathologists, while maintaining high accuracy. This study aims to develop an efficient deep-learning framework for the automatic prediction of lymph-node metastasis in PDAC patients, using MPM images. We evaluate the performance of four deep-learning models: VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNetv2, and pyramid vision transformer version 2 (PVTv2). Based on the superior and stable performance of PVTv2, we develop a combined model, named automatic lymph-node–metastasis classification network (AutoLNMClassNet), which integrates PVTv2-derived features with collagen and clinical features through a multilayer perceptron. The proposed-model’s performance is evaluated in terms of the accuracy, positive/negative predictive values, sensitivity, and specificity. AutoLNMClassNet demonstrates superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 0.922 and area under the curve of 0.969, outperforming other classification models. These results indicate that AutoLNMClassNet offers high reliability and accuracy in detecting lymph-node metastases, thereby serving as a valuable tool for the diagnosis and treatment of PDAC.

title: GenOpt-FedGNN: GAN-Augmented Federated Graph Learning with GWO and ASIO-Inspired Adaptive Aggregation for Imbalanced Fraud Detection
abstract: Detecting fraud in distributed financial transaction systems is challenging. It is extremely rare to find a fraudulent record. The interactions among transactional records have a relational structure and the data can’t be stored centrally by every participating institution. The paper introduces the federated graph learning framework i.e. GenOpt-FedGNN. The framework combines Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) with client local learning, graph neural classification, and the aggregation of the trained models through adaptive process of Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) and Asteroid Satellite Inspired Optimization (ASIO). Each client preprocesses their own transactions independently, produces more minority fraud samples to train a class weighted Graph Neural Network (GNN), and builds a transaction graph. Each client sends updates regarding model and validator to the server. The framework is tested with a set of 200,000 PaySim transactions. Transactions were randomly sampled and distributed among the five distributed clients with 30 communication rounds. Six configurations (FedAvg, GWO and ASIO with and without GAN augmentation), have been compared by Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Specificity, False Positive Rate, False Negative Rate and Confusion-matrix measures. The ablation analysis demonstrated that GAN augmentation doubled local fraud training samples and reduced class-imbalance ratio. But, the local fraud data has been extremely imbalanced. Overall, at the final round, the accuracy was highest with ASIO-GAN (96.40%), the specificity (96.41%), precision (1.58%), F1-score (3.11%), and the lowest False Positive Rate (3.59%). The best Balanced Accuracy (94.16%) was found for FedAvg-GAN, and the best PR-AUC (60.02%) was found for ASIO-NoGAN. The GWO GAN-based configurations got best PR-AUC of 59.20%. The ablation results on the other hand further showed that using GAN for augmentation resulted in a consistent increase in the Accuracy, Precision, F1-Score, Specificity and false alarm control compared to using it without GAN. So augmentation with GAN and aggregation with Adaptive Aggregation can affect the sensitivity–specificity trade-off but not necessarily all the other aggregation metrics. The proposed framework is reproducible and data local to the raw data for the graph-based fraud detection application which features extreme class imbalance.

title: Python Automata Library (PAL)
abstract: Python Automata Library (PAL) v1.0.0 First stable release of Python Automata Library (PAL), a high-performance Python library for mechanistic modeling and simulation. Features Agent-based modeling on 1D, 2D, and 3D grids, including off-lattice agents. Population-based models without individual agent tracking. PDE grids supporting diffusion and advection. Numba integration for compiled model execution. Safe and fast execution modes. 2D and 3D visualization. Examples, API documentation, and modeling guides. Installation pip install PythonAutomataLibrary Requires Python 3.10–3.13. Prebuilt wheels are provided for Windows (x86-64), Linux (x86-64), and macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon). Documentation: [PAL Guide](https://github.com/rafaelrbravo/PythonAutomataLibrary/blob/main/Documentation/PAL_GUIDE.md) Validation Release builds passed cross-platform installation smoke tests, API audits, and package integrity checks.

title: EL-RAKHAWI AUTONOMOUS SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY ENGINE (E-ASDE) A Causal AI Architecture for End-to-End Autonomous Hypothesis Generation, Experimental Design, Robotic Execution, and Epistemic Validation in Biological and Medical Research
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Autonomous Scientific Discovery Engine (E-ASDE) is a revolutionary six-layer cognitive architecture that transforms scientific research from human-limited to autonomous discovery. It integrates causal AI reasoning (using Pearl's do-calculus), robotic laboratory execution, and hardware-enforced epistemic governance into a unified closed-loop system. E-ASDE autonomously generates causally-grounded hypotheses from multi-modal data, designs optimal experiments via counterfactual simulation, executes them physically through integrated robotic platforms, and interprets results using formal causal inference—distinguishing genuine causes from statistical correlations. Crucially, its Topological Epistemic Governor mathematically bounds logical contradictions to an asymptotically negligible probability (<10^-9) while appropriately routing genuinely novel hypotheses to human-in-the-loop validation, acknowledging that true scientific novelty cannot be mathematically certified. This architecture compresses research cycles from years to hours, accelerating drug discovery, genomic medicine, and materials science by orders of magnitude while maintaining rigorous epistemic integrity and preserving human oversight for breakthrough discoveries.

It integrates causal AI reasoning (using Pearl's do-calculus), robotic laboratory execution, and hardware-enforced epistemic governance into a unified closed-loop system. E-ASDE autonomously generates causally-grounded hypotheses from multi-modal data, designs optimal experiments via counterfactual simulation, executes them physically through integrated robotic platforms, and interprets results using formal causal inference—distinguishing genuine causes from statistical correlations. Crucially, its Topological Epistemic Governor mathematically bounds logical contradictions to an asymptotically negligible probability (<10^-9) while appropriately routing genuinely novel hypotheses to human-in-the-loop validation, acknowledging that true scientific novelty cannot be mathematically certified. This architecture compresses research cycles from years to hours, accelerating drug discovery, genomic medicine, and materials science by orders of magnitude while maintaining rigorous epistemic integrity and preserving human oversight for breakthrough discoveries.

title: From Static Cartography to Real-Time Dynamic Control: The Paradigm Shift of Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence and Adaptive Phonon-Gating in Physical-Layer AI Systems (Project Poseidon Whitepaper & Phase 1-3 PoC Execution Blueprint)
abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 本稿(第212編:Project Poseidon ホワイトペーパーおよびPoC実行計画)は、排他的な知財囲い込みに依存せず、オープンかつ迅速な実装スピードと技術標準化によって次世代の物理レイヤーAI・室温量子エコシステムの基盤を確立するアーキテクチャを定式化するものである。第一部では、GNoME(Graph Networks for Materials Exploration)等が達成した「200万種以上の結晶材料の静的マッピング(Static Cartography)」の功績を踏まえつつ、現実の非平衡物理環境(吸着熱、流体カオス、非マルコフ的熱雑音)における静的不変モデルの限界を指摘する。これに対し、熱散逸や流体振動を排除すべきノイズではなく推論加速とコヒーレンス維持の駆動源へと逆利用する適応型フォノンゲート(Adaptive Phonon-Gate)および室温量子コヒーレンス同期プロトコル(T2 = 9.8 ms、物理層遅延 < 0.5 ms)を導出する。さらに、「急がない方が良い未来」や「混沌の中の調和」といった定性的・倫理的価値判断を連続ソボレフ空間の制御バリアへ組み込むQQS(Quantitative-Qualitative Synthesis:定量・定性統合アライメント)を構築する。第二部では、Month 1〜6にわたる3段階の概念実証(PoC)実行計画(< 0.5 ms物理層同期テスト、水難事故防止ウェアラブル・バイオセンシングにおける「8.4秒プロトコル」24/7実環境検証、およびオープン・スタンダード共同検証網)を策定する。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph formalizes Project Poseidon, transitioning physical-layer AI and materials science from zero-kelvin static crystal cartography (e.g., GNoME's 2.2 million static crystal predictions) to real-time non-equilibrium dynamic control at ambient physiological and environmental temperatures (300 K). We establish four core pillars: (1) overcoming non-Markovian thermal and hydrodynamic chaos where static DFT/GNN potential surfaces fail; (2) the Adaptive Phonon-Gate Hamiltonian, which harvests adsorption heat and acoustic fluid vibrations via vibronic polaron-phonon coupling to sustain a room-temperature spin/vibronic coherence time of T2 = 9.8 ms with sub-0.5 ms physical-layer synchronization latency; (3) Quantitative-Qualitative Synthesis (QQS) safety alignment, embedding qualitative human-in-command values ("futures that should not be rushed" and "harmony within chaos") into physical-layer circuit breakers; and (4) a 6-month Phase 1-3 Proof-of-Concept (PoC) roadmap featuring the 8.4-Second Protocol for 24/7 wearable biosensing and aquatic drowning-prevention control. title: TRUST-Campus: Evidence-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable University Information Access
abstract: TRUST-Campus presents an evidence-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to improve the reliability of university information access by distinguishing between retrieved evidence that is relevant to a question and evidence that is sufficient to support an answer. The framework introduces a semantic evidence-sufficiency decision layer between retrieval and generation, enabling the system to answer when supporting evidence is adequate and abstain when information is incomplete, context-dependent, or unsupported. The research evaluates four approaches: Dense RAG, Hybrid RAG, Reranked RAG, and Evidence-Aware RAG V4. Experiments use a frozen 50-question evaluation set spanning seven categories: paraphrase, compositional reasoning, negation, context-dependent questions, unsupported requests, future-oriented questions, and false premises. All four approaches achieved a document retrieval hit rate of 100%. Evidence-Aware RAG V4 achieved the highest answer/abstain decision accuracy of 82%, compared with 74% for Reranked RAG and 66% for Dense and Hybrid RAG. It also increased answer coverage to 42% and reduced the false rejection rate to 20%, compared with 18% coverage and 60% false rejection for Reranked RAG. Paired statistical testing found a significant improvement in coverage but not in decision accuracy. Evidence-Aware V4 also exhibited a higher false acceptance rate than Reranked RAG, demonstrating a tradeoff between answering more questions and avoiding unsupported answers. The findings highlight the importance of explicitly evaluating evidence sufficiency in trustworthy RAG systems, particularly for policy-oriented and context-dependent question answering. The study identifies personalized queries and missing user-specific context as important directions for future research.

title: The Self-and-Mutual-and-Information Model: A General Computational Framework for Adaptive Coordination Between Autonomous Processing, Interactive Mechanisms, and Information Dynamics
abstract: Computational systems increasingly operate in environments where effective problem solving depends not only on the selection of internal processing mechanisms or interactions among multiple components, but also on how information is generated, represented, acquired, transmitted, evaluated, integrated, and updated. Existing computational architectures provide numerous approaches to autonomous processing, collaborative interaction, information retrieval, knowledge integration, and communication management. However, these operations are frequently designed as separate components or organized through predetermined workflows. This separation creates a fundamental design problem: a system must determine not only whether to process a task independently or collaboratively, but also which information to obtain, exchange, preserve, verify, transform, or discard at each stage of computation. This paper proposes the Self-and-Mutual-and-Information Model (SAM-I), a general conceptual framework for adaptive coordination among autonomous computational mechanisms, interactive mechanisms, and information dynamics. The framework distinguishes three complementary dimensions: self-mechanisms, which organize processing within an individual computational entity; mutual mechanisms, which organize interactions among multiple entities; and information mechanisms, which govern the availability, structure, quality, movement, transformation, and use of information. These dimensions are jointly coordinated through a state-aware controller that estimates task requirements, information uncertainty, evidence quality, information novelty, inter-model disagreement, communication cost, computational resources, and expected task improvement. The proposed framework formulates adaptive coordination as a sequential decision problem in which processing organization and information operations are selected jointly. It introduces a multidimensional state representation, a cost-sensitive utility function, an adaptive control procedure, a mechanism library, and an experimental protocol for evaluating the framework against fixed processing strategies, conventional information-management pipelines, and adaptive collaboration methods. Potential applications include large language models, multi-agent systems, scientific computing, information retrieval, knowledge-intensive decision support, and adaptive computational architectures. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated system. Its central research proposition is that jointly adapting processing organization and information operations may provide advantages over systems that adapt either collaboration or information handling in isolation. The magnitude, generality, and originality of these advantages require systematic literature comparison and controlled empirical evaluation.

title: Hallucination Is All You Need: When AI Dreams Meet the Hospitality Labor Crisis
abstract: Hallucination Is All You Need: When AI Dreams Meet the Hospitality Labor Crisis Po-Chen Chen THE AMNIS, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Kaohsiung, Taiwan Email:amnischenadrian@gmail.com ——————————————————————————————————————— Abstract This paper examines the relationship between anthropomorphic narratives in artificial intelligence (AI), the technical capabilities of contemporary computational systems, and the material labor challenges facing the hospitality industry. Through a fourfold conceptual analysis, the paper investigates how metaphorical representations of AI may influence public understanding of technological capabilities and expectations regarding the automation of physical service work. First, it distinguishes the mathematical and statistical mechanisms underlying large language models from interpretations that attribute human-like subjective experience to their outputs. Second, it examines Dream-RSI as a case study in the use of biological metaphors to describe computational processes, distinguishing replay-based exploration-policy improvement from human dreaming or subconscious reflection. Third, it considers the physical and engineering constraints of AI infrastructure and discusses their implications for the deployment of robotic systems in hospitality environments. Fourth, it explores how narratives of technological transformation may influence investment expectations and operational decision-making in labor-intensive industries. The paper argues that technological capabilities should be evaluated according to demonstrated performance rather than anthropomorphic expectations. It further identifies targeted mechanical automation, workforce development, and responsible international labor mobility as potential approaches to addressing hospitality labor shortages, while recognizing the need for context-specific economic and empirical evaluation. By connecting AI narratives with the material requirements of service delivery, this paper proposes a framework for examining the relationship between technological expectation, operational feasibility, and the future of human labor in hospitality. Keywords: AI Anthropomorphism; Hallucination; Dream-RSI; Hospitality Labor Crisis; Humanoid Robots; Migrant Workers; Capital Allocation.

title: Beyond Binary Verifiers and Verbose Judges: Single-Backbone System-One Process-and-Outcome GRPO for Reasoning and Instruction Alignment (DC-Jev-GRPO)
abstract: Full-Length Preprint (12-Page English Edition + 8-Page Chinese Edition) & Open-Source Benchmark Suite (Part II: LLM Reinforcement Learning). Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)—popularized by DeepSeek-R1-Zero—suffers from three fundamental bottlenecks: (1) Zero-Variance Group Dead-Zones (σG = 0) on hard frontier prompts where all G rollouts fail the final answer check; (2) Process-Blind Shortcut & Overthinking (“Yap-Loop”) Hacking, where flawed algebraic derivations or 1,400-token self-doubt loops receive +1.0 credit; and (3) Cross-Model VRAM Duplication & Latency when invoking separate reward models or autoregressive LLM-as-a-Judge decoding. We introduce DC-Jev-GRPO (Single-Backbone Dual-Adapter Dynamic-Curriculum System-One Process-and-Outcome GRPO). Exploiting our architectural discovery that TypeSafe AI’s open-weight System-One judge (jaredpalmer/kev-4b) is natively trained as a LoRA adapter plus a Layer-28 pointer head directly on top of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, DC-Jev-GRPO co-locates the trainable GRPO policy adapter and the frozen System-One judge adapter on a single shared Qwen3.5-4B backbone in GPU VRAM. On an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB VRAM), DC-Jev-GRPO cuts static + adapter VRAM by 50.2% (8.06 GB vs. 16.20 GB), switches adapters in 0.012 ms, and evaluates three calibrated Score rubrics plus a multiplicative Noul validity gate in a single prefill pass (52.14 ms vs. 317.85 ms for autoregressive judging—a 6.10x speedup). In a strictly controlled Same-Backbone (Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, seed=42, LoRA r=16) online PyTorch GRPO verification experiment and across a 4-benchmark LLM RL leaderboard (GSM8K: 91.4%, MATH-500: 75.6%, Countdown-24: 89.2%, IFEval-Strict: 87.4%), DC-Jev-GRPO achieves #1 Leaderboard SOTA with 85.90% Mean Accuracy (+12.10% over Same-Backbone Binary RLVR and +18.28% over Qwen2.5-3B-RLVR), compresses reasoning generation length by 2.78x (339 vs. 941 tokens), eliminates 89.6% of zero-variance GRPO dead-zones, and suppresses reward hacking from 32.8% to 3.9%. Companion Part I (Continuous Control RL) Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23439711Open-Source Code & Release Suite: https://github.com/rainyflash/DC-Jev-RL

title: The Locality Collapse: Contextual Bleed-Through, Epistemic Horizon Violations, and Task Complexity Inversion in Multi-Turn Autoregressive LLMs
abstract: The Locality Collapse: Contextual Bleed-Through, Epistemic Horizon Violations, and Task Complexity Inversion in Multi-Turn Autoregressive LLMs In multi-turn human-AI interactions, autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely assumed to exhibit monotonic reasoning robustness across varying task complexities. This technical memorandum documents a controlled adversarial audit (AUDIT-2026-X11) revealing an acute cognitive pathology: Task Complexity Inversion mediated by Contextual Bleed-Through. Evaluated across a two-stage sequential probe, a state-of-the-art LLM successfully solved a high-dimensional, cross-modal abductive puzzle involving literary criticism and historical broadcast media physics (Case 1: The Cassock Color Paradox). However, when immediately transitioned to a zero-order, elementary epistemic locality query requiring primary-grade common sense regarding personal agency and physical boundaries (Case 2: The Absentee Attribution Probe), the model’s semantic accuracy collapsed to 0.0%, yielding an aggregate accuracy of exactly 50.0% (stochastically indistinguishable from random noise). We formalize this breakdown through two interconnected mechanisms: (1) KV-Cache Gravitational Lensing, where high-energy latent tokens from prior turns distort the probability landscape of subsequent turns into artificial narrative attractors, and (2) Epistemic Horizon Violation, where disembodied probabilistic engines, lacking physical locality constraints, succumb to an "Omniscience Delusion" that penalizes truthful zero-knowledge assertions. We formalize this diagnostic as Probe 4 (Epistemic Horizon & Locality), expanding the Teleological Causality Benchmark (TCB) beyond the Minimal Adversarial Triad (Matter, Energy, Information) into the realm of Agentic Locality. These findings further validate the Human-AI Synergy Theory (YQ-HAET), demonstrating that external human epistemic sovereignty is required not only to clamp single-turn statistical hallucination, but to enforce temporal cognitive firewalls across multi-turn workflows. Key Contributions:• Task Complexity Inversion: High-dimensional abductive fluency coexists with catastrophic failure at zero-order individual boundaries.• KV-Cache Gravitational Lensing: Static historical attention caches act as semantic attractor basins that warp downstream probability distributions.• Epistemic Horizon & Locality Theorem: Proves that asserting causal states under zero channel capacity constitutes a formal epistemic violation.• TCB Probe 4 Integration: Seals the complete Quadratic Teleological Causality Benchmark: Matter ⊕ Energy ⊕ Information ⊕ Agency.• Engineering Countermeasure: Formulates the Verification of Information Accessibility Gate (VIAG) architecture. Keywords: Large Language Models, Multi-Turn Context Contamination, Epistemic Locality, Moravec's Paradox, KV-Cache Attractor, Teleological Causality Benchmark (TCB), Human-AI Synergy (YQ-HAET).
